summary: The study describes the preparation of Ta2O5 and TiO2-based nanostructures using atomic layer deposition (ALD) on porous alumina membranes. The nanostructures include nanotubes and nanorods, with applications in photocatalysis and as catalyst supports. The process involves ALD of Ta2O5 and TiO2 on self-supporting and Si-supported thin-film membranes, with the possibility of modifying the nanostructures by depositing Pt nanoparticles inside the nanotubes.
evidence: The text states that 'Ta2O5 and TiO2 thin films were deposited on the pore walls of porous alumina membranes' and 'the Ta2O5 nanotubes were prepared by 1000 ALD cycles of Ta(OEt)5 and H2O' and 'the TiO2 nanotubes were prepared by 1000 ALD cycles of TiCl4 and H2O'. It also mentions that 'Pt nanoparticles were deposited inside the Ta2O5 and TiO2 nanotubes' and 'the TiO2 nanotubes showed photocatalytic activity in methylene blue degradation under UV illumination'.
